name: Silver Spigot
notes: not_found: Silver Spigot Cocktail Lounge is a dive bar (dartboards, pool tables, jukebox) at 2221 Morena Blvd. Its own domain silverspigot.com 301s to quinnslighthouse.com/press2.html, which actually serves cloaked/hijacked content (a Shopee e-commerce JS bundle, unrelated to any restaurant) -- a hijacked domain per playbook rule, barred outright. No ordering platform presence found (DoorDash/Grubhub/UberEats search turned up nothing). restaurantguru.com gives only a per-person price range ($10-$20), no per-item prices. menupix.com and Yelp both 403'd a curl fetch; weeblyte.com (a barred farm domain) also surfaced in search and was not used. Reviews describe it as serving snacks/small food under $15 but no source anywhere lists actual priced food items. Treating as a bar with no publishable per-item menu.

name: Saddle Bar
notes: not_found: Saddle Bar (Solana Beach) is a dive bar. Its own About page and a quoted customer review state explicitly: "They don't serve food but don't care if you bring in your own. You can even order from the Pillbox two doors up and their servers will bring the grub in the bar to you." No menu link anywhere on the site (checked homepage nav, wp-json pages). This is a drink-only bar with no per-item food prices to record.

name: The Clubhouse Grill
notes: First-party PDF menu from the resort's own site (Fairmont Grand Del Mar / granddelmar.com), filename dated 8.12.24, read with pdftotext -layout. The live URL 404s directly but the identical file (same content hash) is archived by the Wayback Machine across Apr 2025, Aug 2025 and Feb 2026 crawls, so it is treated as current, not stale; fetched via https://web.archive.org/web/20260216134318/<url>. The live site also links a menumodo.com embedded viewer (outlet 12128, menu 247521) for the same restaurant but that widget is fully client-rendered JS with no server-side data -- not usable without a browser, so this PDF was used instead. A stale SinglePlatform listing (Baja Fish Tacos $12) was checked and rejected: it undercuts this PDF's prices by roughly 2x with no clean fee ratio, which per the staleness rule means the SinglePlatform copy is simply an old page, not evidence of a markup. Categories reached: Starters, Mains, Salads, Dessert, weekly Daily Specials, Cocktails, Wine (red/white/sparkling/rose), Beer & Seltzer, Draft -- this is the restaurant's single combined lunch/dinner/bar menu (open 7:30am-6pm daily; the resort site separately mentions breakfast items served on guest patios/rooms, which is not covered by this PDF and not found priced elsewhere). Two-tier drink prices on the PDF (e.g. Longball John Daly $12/$20) recorded at the lower/base price with a note.

name: Contodo Fresh Mexican Eats
notes: Restaurant's own site (tacorestaurantsandiego.com, address confirmed 111 S Meadowbrook Dr matches work list -- domain name mismatch is just marketing branding, not a different business) prices nothing itself; it only teases Tacos/Burritos/Carne Asada Fries with 'read more' links and points to Grubhub, Zmenu and Seamless for ordering. Grubhub, Seamless and Zmenu were all unreadable without a browser (JS wall / 403). Found DoorDash's marketplace listing instead, which server-renders a full schema.org Menu JSON-LD (tier 3, medium at best per source ladder). Ran the markup divisor test (1.04/1.10/1.15/1.17/1.20/1.25/1.30) across all 46 priced items excluding the duplicate 'Most Ordered' showcase section -- no divisor lands more than 4/46 items on a round or .95 value, so this is ordinary odd-cent psychological pricing (dominated by .95 endings), not a delivery markup. No first-party dine-in artefact (PDF/photo/board) was found to cross-check against, so confidence stays medium rather than high. Categories reached: Tacos, Specialty Tacos, Burritos, Breakfast, Extras, Drinks, Sides -- this covers everything the restaurant's own site names as its specialties (tacos, burritos, carne asada fries -- fries/chips items appear under Extras). The 'Most Ordered' section was dropped as a duplicate of items already listed under their real sections.

name: Lucca's Pizzeria and Market
blocked: no reliable price source: the restaurant's own Slice storefront (luccaspizzeriamarket.com) carries a mathematically perfect, uniform 20% markup, and the DoorDash listing that could have corrected it disagrees with Slice by an inconsistent amount item-to-item with no clean ratio -- need either a dine-in artefact (printed menu/PDF/board photo) or a browser to read Yelp's photo gallery (403s to curl and WebFetch) or the Clover COLO2 storefront (clover.com/online-ordering/luccas-pizza--market-san-diego-2, a client-rendered React SPA with no server-side data)
notes: The restaurant's own domain runs a Slice ordering widget that server-renders its full menu (73 priced items across Pizza, Antipasti, Wings & Appetizers, Fries, Insalate/Salads, Calzones, Sandwiches, Pasta, Just For Kids, Desserts -- looks like a complete pizzeria menu by section shape). Ran the standard markup divisor test: dividing every one of the 73 Slice prices by exactly 1.2 lands on a whole dollar 73/73 times (100%), which is the textbook clean-markup signature from the playbook (the Pacific Pizza case) -- this is a 20% online-ordering uplift baked into the restaurant's own storefront, not the wall price. Went looking for a second source to recover the true price: DoorDash's marketplace listing (schema.org Menu JSON-LD) has the same restaurant's menu in whole-dollar prices, but comparing matching items by name shows NO consistent ratio to Slice -- e.g. The Boarder Pizza, Amante Della Carne, BBQ/Buffalo Chicken Pizza and Lasagna are all exactly Slice/1.1; Create Your Own Pizza and Italian Sandwich are exactly Slice/1.2; Meatball Calzone and Ham & Cheese Calzone are Slice/1.14; Gyro Salad, 4 Cheese Pizza, Fettuccine Alfredo and Spaghetti are actually HIGHER on DoorDash than on Slice. Running the same divisor test on DoorDash's own 56 items in isolation finds no clean signature either (best was 1.2 at 26.8%, which the playbook calls noise, not a markup). So neither source's prices can be trusted as-is, and they can't be reconciled against each other -- textbook 'disagreement with no clean ratio is unresolved, not resolvable.' No PDF or dine-in photo was found through search; Yelp (which sometimes carries a dated menu photo) returned 403 to both curl and WebFetch, and the only other ordering surface (Clover, via clover.com/online-ordering/luccas-pizza--market-san-diego-2) redirects into Clover's COLO2 React SPA with no server-rendered data reachable by curl. Recording nothing rather than picking a side or dividing out the markup.

name: Slice House
blocked: no reliable price source: DoorDash carries a mathematically perfect, uniform 15% markup on this store, and every first-party alternative is a client-rendered app unreadable without a browser -- need either a browser to read the restaurant's actual ordering widget (a Paytronix Nuxt.js SPA at slicehouse.orderexperience.net, embedded on slicehouse.com) or to get past a 403 on api.slicehouse.com/menu (exists, but rejects a plain curl request -- likely needs auth/session headers a browser would supply)
notes: This is Slice House by Tony Gemignani, a small pizza chain; this location (2100 Kettner Blvd Ste 1400, San Diego) opened May 2025 and its address on DoorDash matches the work list exactly. The restaurant's own site (slicehouse.com) is a JS SPA with zero server-rendered content; tracing its JS bundle found the real ordering backend is Paytronix at slicehouse.orderexperience.net, itself a Nuxt.js app that only prints 'Loading...' server-side -- no menu data reachable by curl. Fell back to DoorDash's marketplace listing (schema.org Menu JSON-LD), which has 8 sections / 79 priced items (Specials, Antipasti, Italian Specialties, Medium 12in/XL 20in New York Style, Grandma 12x12, Detroit 9x12, plus a duplicate 'Most Ordered' showcase excluded from the count) -- but running the standard markup divisor test found every single one of the 79 items (100%) divides cleanly by exactly 1.15, the textbook clean-markup signature. Checked whether Grubhub's listing (a different company from DoorDash) might carry the untouched price, but Grubhub's page is entirely client-rendered with no data in the initial HTML, same as it was for a different restaurant earlier in this batch. api.slicehouse.com/menu exists (returns 403, not 404) but rejects a bare curl request. No PDF or dine-in photo found through search for this brand-new location. Recording nothing rather than reporting DoorDash's marked-up numbers or a divided-out guess.
